ajv2.sub: Integrated Soul Assessment — 4 Dimensions of Self
ajv2.greeting_desc: Allah has guided you here. Today, let's do muhasabah together — like an honest, caring friend.
ajv2.tentang_desc: Soul Audit is more than a questionnaire. It's an integrated muhasabah — honestly assessing 4 dimensions of yourself, rooted in the Quran and the Soul School tradition.
ajv2.quran_rad_28: Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.
ajv2.foundation_short: Modern life focuses on the body (gym, diet, sleep) but neglects the soul. The result: healthy body, empty heart — anxiety, depression, loss of direction. The Islamic solution: INTEGRATED audit. When the RUH (root) heals, everything heals.
ajv2.foundation_raga: Your body is a trust (amanah) from Allah. It is the foundation of all spiritual practice. The Prophet SAW said: 'Your body has rights over you.' A healthy body makes it easier for the soul to remember Allah.
ajv2.foundation_hati: The heart is the command center. When the Ruh is alive with zikir, the heart becomes calm and grateful. Allah says: 'Verily, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.' (Ar-Ra'd: 28)
ajv2.foundation_akal: A clear mind is born from a calm heart and a living Ruh. When the heart is filled with anxiety, the mind cannot think clearly. Zikir clarifies the mind.
ajv2.foundation_ruh: The Ruh is the root. When the Ruh is alive with zikir, the whole being follows. Shaikh Abdul Qadir Jilani taught: 'When the Qalb is alive with the remembrance of Allah, the whole being becomes alive.'
ajv2.cascade_desc: When RUH (root) heals → Heart calms → Mind clears → Body strengthens.
ajv2.cascade_root_desc: Heal this first — it will positively impact your entire being.
ajv2.analisis_desc: Ruh is the root of the soul's tree. When Ruh is weak, it affects the entire self — the heart becomes restless, the mind becomes foggy, the body feels the strain.

a1.soalan: During that prayer — at what moment did your thoughts begin to wander?
a1.ikutan: What appeared in your mind at that moment?

a2.soalan: What was the first thing you thought about after the prayer's salam?
a2.ikutan: Was that thing more important than Allah at that moment?

a3.soalan: Was there a whisper of 'finish the prayer quickly, I have other things to do' during that prayer?
a3.ikutan: That whisper — where did it come from?

a4.soalan: How many times did you need to 'pull back' your thoughts to the prayer during that rak'ah?
a4.ikutan: What kept pulling your thoughts away at that time?

a5.soalan: Did you feel watched by Allah throughout that prayer?
a5.ikutan: If yes — why were there still distracting thoughts?

a6.soalan: What most easily steals your heart's presence during prayer?
a6.ikutan: How long has that thing been disturbing you?

a7.soalan: Did you ever forget how many rak'ahs you had completed during that prayer?
a7.ikutan: What were you thinking about at that moment?

a8.soalan: Imagine a shaytan saying: 'Finish the prayer quickly.' Did you hear that voice during that prayer?
a8.ikutan: How did that voice feel — subtle or strong?

a9.soalan: Was there a feeling of heaviness about getting up to pray beforehand?

a10.soalan: After the prayer — did you feel something was 'missed' or 'incomplete'?

a11.soalan: During that prayer — were you aware of the exact moment your heart began to wander?
a11.ikutan: How did it feel when you realised your heart had strayed far?

a12.soalan: What dreams or future plans appeared during that prayer?
a12.ikutan: Where did those thoughts come from during prayer time?

a13.soalan: Was there a moment during that prayer when you felt 'very far' from Allah?

a14.soalan: When was the last time you prayed with no distracting thoughts at all?
a14.ikutan: What was different then compared to today?

a15.soalan: Did your phone or notifications cross your mind during that prayer?
a15.ikutan: How strong was that pull during the prayer?

a16.soalan: After the salam — how many seconds before you picked up your phone?
a16.ikutan: What drove you to do that so quickly?

a17.soalan: Was there a voice in your head saying your prayer was not accepted or not good enough?
a17.ikutan: Where did that voice come from — and did you believe it?

a18.soalan: Rushing in prayer — for the sake of what?
a18.ikutan: What was more important than Allah at that moment?

a19.soalan: Was there a moment during that prayer when you felt Allah was very close?
a19.ikutan: What happened after that beautiful moment?

a20.soalan: If shaytan had a KPI to disrupt your prayer — did he succeed today?
a20.ikutan: What was his most effective strategy against you?

b1.soalan: Was there a part of you that 'didn't want' to pray beforehand?
b1.ikutan: What excuse did the nafs give you at that time?

b2.soalan: That prayer — was it merely fulfilling an obligation or a genuine desire to meet Allah?
b2.ikutan: Honestly — which more accurately describes your prayer?

b3.soalan: Were you satisfied with the quality of that prayer?
b3.ikutan: If satisfied — is that a sign of success or a nafs that is easily content?

b4.soalan: How many times today did you prioritise your own desires over Allah's commands?
b4.ikutan: Who won more today — you or your nafs?

b5.soalan: Was Fajr prayer today done with full awareness or merely performed?
b5.ikutan: What is the difference for you between those two states?

b6.soalan: What did you crave more — rest or prayer — before that prayer?
b6.ikutan: That is the nafs speaking. What does your soul say?

b7.soalan: Did you pray out of fear of sin or out of love for Allah?
b7.ikutan: Which was stronger in your heart during that prayer?

b8.soalan: After prayer — did you feel better or exactly the same?
b8.ikutan: If the same — what might be preventing the prayer from having an effect?

b9.soalan: When was the last time you cried during prayer or felt deeply moved?
b9.ikutan: What was different then compared to today's prayer?

b10.soalan: Was there a feeling of pride after prayer — 'alhamdulillah I've prayed'?
b10.ikutan: That pride — from a grateful soul or from a nafs that feels it has done enough?

b11.soalan: What do you most enjoy doing after prayer?
b11.ikutan: Does it bring you closer to or further from Allah?

b12.soalan: Do you pray the same way as 10 years ago?
b12.ikutan: If yes — what has changed in your heart compared to your prayer back then?

b13.soalan: Nafs always calls to evil — as Allah says in Surah Yusuf. Today, what did your nafs call you to?
b13.ikutan: How many times did you hear that call — and how many times did you comply?

b14.soalan: Did the prayer change how you treat others afterwards?
b14.ikutan: If not — why hasn't prayer yet impacted your behaviour?

b15.soalan: What does your nafs dislike most about the practice of prayer?
b15.ikutan: That is precisely what most needs to be guarded — why?

b16.soalan: Are you more easily drawn to what the nafs desires than to what Allah commands?
b16.ikutan: Give one example that happened today.

b17.soalan: After prayer — how quickly did you return to old habits?
b17.ikutan: What pulled you back so fast?

b18.soalan: Is there something you knew was wrong but still did today?
b18.ikutan: Who won that battle — your conscience or your nafs?

b19.soalan: If nafs is the enemy within — what is its most effective weapon against you?
b19.ikutan: When is it strongest — morning, afternoon, or night?

b20.soalan: Allah says nafs always calls to evil. Today — what evil did nafs call you to?
b20.ikutan: Were you aware of it while it was happening or only after?

c1.soalan: Imagine there is a fortress that closes all doors for shaytan. Do you want to know this fortress?
c1.ikutan: What has been stopping you from seeking it all this time?

c2.soalan: The awliya of Allah practise a special zikir to ward off shaytan from outside and nafs from within. Do you want to know this zikir?
c2.ikutan: What do you hope will change if you practise it?

c3.soalan: If there is a remedy for the two diseases blocking your mission in this world — do you want to know this remedy?
c3.ikutan: What makes you confident or doubtful about it?

c4.soalan: Allah declares that zikir is the most magnificent of deeds. Have you ever wondered why?
c4.ikutan: What answer have you found so far?

c5.soalan: Have you ever experienced a prayer that was truly calm — no shaytan interference, no nafs persuasion?
c5.ikutan: Would you like that feeling to be the experience of every prayer?

c6.soalan: If you could add only one practice to your life that would have the greatest impact — what would it be?
c6.ikutan: What is stopping you from practising it now?

c7.soalan: What is the single biggest change you want to see in your prayer in the next 30 days?
c7.ikutan: What do you feel is the first step to take?

c8.soalan: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'For everything there is a polish, and the polish of the heart is the remembrance of Allah.' What does this mean to you?
c8.ikutan: When did you last truly polish your heart?

c9.soalan: If your soul could speak — what would it ask of you today?
c9.ikutan: What is stopping you from giving it that?

c10.soalan: What is the one thing about your relationship with Allah that you most urgently want to improve?
c10.ikutan: What is the greatest obstacle to be overcome?
